abstract.t: This document defines the Agent Transfer Protocol (AGTP): a transfer protocol for AI agent traffic. AGTP carries agent identity, authority, delegation, and attribution as protocol elements of every exchange, on an eighteen-method floor of intent-named methods, over TCP/TLS or QUIC on IANA-assigned port 4480 and the IANA-registered agtp:// URI scheme. The method vocabulary beyond the floor, the path grammar, and the endpoint contract are specified in [AGTP-METHODS]; runtime negotiation of endpoints is specified in [AGTP-RCNS]; the agent identity document in [AGTP-IDDOC]; transport bindings in [AGTP-BINDINGS]. Version 10 adds per-request proof of possession, so that a verified identity document and a live sender are bound by signature; specifies the Delegation-Chain header with pre- authorization semantics (per-hop scope attenuation checked at mint and at verify, parent re-verification at each hop, depth and cycle limits, and defined failure behavior); maps the delegation model onto the WIMSE chain convention; resolves the 262 and 455 status codes by obtainability; adds structured failure fields to the status code model, states the protocol's position in the transfer-protocol vocabulary throughout, and moves module material to companion specifications so that this document carries the protocol and only the protocol. AGTP is designed to compose with existing agent frameworks, which keep their own semantics and development paths.
